title: [bug] Enumerate hidden directories on linux
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi, I'm using in my code
```
readDir(path, { dir: BaseDirectory.Home, recursive: false });
```
from module "fs" and there is impossible to specify all subdirectories in "allowlist" -> "scope"

"**" can browse non-hidden directories like  
```
"$HOME/**/*.*"
```
, but not hidden directories. 
".**" is not accepted by tauri. And print error:
```
thread 'main' panicked at 'error while running tauri application: GlobPattern(PatternError { pos: 10, msg: "recursive wildcards must form a single path component" })', src/main.rs:52:10
```

I think all the hidden, non-hidden directories can be allowed by e.g.: 
```
$ echo {.**,**}/{.**,**}/{.*,*}
```

I haven't found a way, how to do this. I need to find all files across all the directories.


### Reproduction

In description. You can try search e.g. directory with .git directory

### Expected behavior

Enumerate hidden directories.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
In the next release, there will be an option to specify `require_literal_leading_dot` so you will be able to do this:
```rs
"scope": {
	"allow": ["$HOME/**"],
	"require_literal_leading_dot": false,
}
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Sorry, which version it will be? I can't find a commit. I have done upgrade of the project and nothing changed

Also, I didn't understand the construction:
```
"scope": {
	"allow": ["$HOME/**"],
	"require_literal_leading_dot": false,
}
```

Does it mean this will work for my purposes?
```
"scope": {
	"allow": [
          "$HOME/**/.*",
          "$HOME/**/*"],
	"require_literal_leading_dot": true,
}
```

or this?
```
"scope": {
	"allow": [
          "$HOME/{.**,**}/{.**,**}/{.*,*}"
        ],
	"require_literal_leading_dot": true,
}

```

I need to get access for every subfolder in directory, regardless they are hidden (with . prefix) or not.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
This is available in `1.4` and this should be enough for your usage:
```json
"scope": {
	"allow": ["$HOME/**"],
	"require_literal_leading_dot": false,
}
```

found the issue and it is my bad, sorry about that, the config should be: 
```json
"scope": {
	"allow": ["$HOME/**"],
	"requireLiteralLeadingDot": false,
}
```

notice the camelCase
